name: The Great Flood
description: Universal motif of a catastrophic flood sent by divine powers, with a chosen survivor preserving life

name: Creation from Primordial Chaos
description: The cosmos emerges from a formless void or primordial waters through divine action

name: The World Tree
description: A cosmic tree connecting different realms of existence (heaven, earth, underworld)

name: The Dying and Rising God
description: A deity who dies and is reborn, often linked to agricultural cycles

name: Journey to the Underworld
description: A hero or deity descends to the realm of the dead and returns transformed

name: The Hero's Quest
description: A hero undertakes a perilous journey, faces trials, and returns with a boon

name: The Thunder God
description: A powerful deity who wields thunder and lightning, often the chief or champion god

name: The Sky Father
description: A supreme male sky deity, linguistically connected across Indo-European traditions (*Dyeus)

name: The Earth Mother
description: A maternal earth goddess associated with fertility, agriculture, and nurturing

name: The Trickster
description: A cunning, rule-breaking figure who disrupts the social order but often brings gifts

name: The Divine Weapon
description: A weapon of supernatural power wielded by a god or hero (Mjölnir, Vajra, Thunderbolt)

name: Death and Rebirth of Seasons
description: Mythological explanation for seasonal changes through divine death and resurrection

name: The Cosmic Axis
description: A central axis connecting earth and heaven — a mountain, pillar, or tree

name: The Culture Hero
description: A figure who brings essential knowledge, tools, or customs to humanity

name: Theft of Fire
description: A hero steals fire from the gods to give to humanity, often suffering punishment
